gloss: to be thirsty; to get thirsty

definitions.gloss: to be thirsty; to get thirsty; to have a dry throat
definitions.explanation: The standard expression for feeling thirsty. Literally means 'the throat dries out.' This is the natural way to express thirst in Japanese, rather than using a single adjective.

examples.japanese: ⟦{運動|うんどう}→運動：00821_undou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}く。
{喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}いた⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦コンビニ→コンビニ：01081_konbini⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{冷|つめ}たい→冷たい：00681_tsumetai⟧⟦お{茶|ちゃ}→お茶：00576_ocha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I was thirsty, so I bought a cold tea at the convenience store.

notes:
The standard Japanese expression for being thirsty. Literally '⟦{喉|のど}→喉：00977_nodo⟧ (throat) ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ (subject marker) ⟦{渇|かわ}く→渇く：10965_kawaku⟧ (to dry out).' Japanese expresses thirst through this phrase rather than a single adjective. The past form {喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}いた is very common in conversation to say 'I'm thirsty.'

USAGE:
The kanji ⟦{渇|かわ}く→渇く：10965_kawaku⟧ means to become parched or dry from lack of moisture. Note the difference from ⟦{乾|かわ}く→乾く：00786_kawaku⟧ (to dry, to become dry), which is used for objects like laundry.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}いた: I'm thirsty (past/resultative)
- ⟦{喉|のど}→喉：00977_nodo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧カラカラ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{渇|かわ}く→渇く：10965_kawaku⟧: to be extremely thirsty (throat bone-dry)
- ⟦{喉|のど}→喉：00977_nodo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{渇|かわ}き→渇き：08251_kawaki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{潤|うるお}す→潤す：08249_uruosu⟧: to quench one's thirst

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦お{腹|なか}→お腹：00805_onaka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{空|す}く: to be hungry — the parallel expression for hunger
- ⟦{喉|のど}→喉：00977_nodo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{乾燥|かんそう}→乾燥：00184_kansou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: for the throat to be dry — medical/physical dryness, not thirst
